stories.headline: Anthropic accuses Alibaba of largest-ever distillation attack, 28.8M Claude exchanges via 25K fake accounts

key_facts.fact: Anthropic accused Alibaba of waging the largest known distillation attack against its Claude models, telling US senators and White House officials that operators linked to Alibaba's Qwen AI lab used nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to extract Claude's capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: telling senators and White House officials that operators linked to Alibaba's Qwen AI lab used nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to extract Claude's capabilities between April and June

key_facts.fact: The campaign ran between April 22 and June 5, 2026, and generated more than 28.8 million exchanges with Claude through almost 25,000 fraudulent accounts.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said the campaign was conducted between April 22 and June 5, 2026, and generated more than 28.8 million exchanges with Claude through almost 25,000 fraudulent accounts.

key_facts.fact: The campaign targeted Claude's most commercially valuable skills, software engineering and agentic reasoning, and Anthropic said it was a way to accelerate China's ability to reach Anthropic's advanced Mythos Preview capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said in the letter that distillation is a way to help accelerate China's ability to reach Anthropic's advanced Mythos Preview capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The letter, dated June 10, was sent to Senators Tim Scott and Elizabeth Warren, chair and ranking member of the US Senate Banking Committee, ahead of a scheduled AI hearing.
key_facts.excerpt: The letter, dated June 10, was sent to Senators Tim Scott and Elizabeth Warren, the chair and ranking member, respectively, of the US Senate Banking Committee, ahead of a scheduled hearing on AI.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic warned that adversarial distillation lets Chinese labs replicate frontier AI at a fraction of the training cost, that such models often lack safety guardrails, and urged the Trump administration to clarify antitrust guidelines, maintain chip export controls, and penalize firms that use the technique.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic warned that adversarial distillation lets Chinese labs replicate frontier AI at a fraction of the training cost, and that models built this way often lack safety guardrails.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba fell about 5% in Hong Kong after the accusation, taking its year-to-date decline to 33%, while Xiaomi and Baidu fell more than 3%.
key_facts.excerpt: ANTHROPIC accused Chinese technology giant Alibaba of waging a large-scale effort to "illicitly" access its Claude artificial intelligence model using thousands of fraudulent accounts

stories.headline: Mirendil, founded by ex-Anthropic researchers, raises $200M seed at $1B valuation to build self-improving AI R&D

key_facts.fact: Mirendil, a San Francisco AI lab founded by former Anthropic researchers, raised $200 million in seed funding at a valuation of roughly $1 billion, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins, with Nvidia participating among other investors.
key_facts.excerpt: AI startup Mirendil raised $200 million in seed funding at a $1 billion valuation, one of the largest AI seed rounds to date... The round was co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins, with NVIDIA participating as an investor.

key_facts.fact: The company is training frontier models that are expert at AI research and engineering, designed to loop over research and engineering problems autonomously and make progress without human intervention.
key_facts.excerpt: Mirendil is building a system that can help anyone do AI work: they train frontier models that are expert at AI R&D and build the product around it. The system is meant to loop over research and engineering problems more autonomously, and make more and more progress without human intervention.

key_facts.fact: The founding team consists of 20 researchers and engineers from frontier labs including Anthropic, xAI, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI; co-founders are Behnam Neyshabur, Harsh Mehta, Shayan Salehian, and Tara Rezaei.
key_facts.excerpt: Our founding team consists of 20 researchers and engineers from frontier institutions including Anthropic, xAI, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Mirendil's goal is to democratize frontier AI R&D so that labs working in drug discovery, chemistry, biology, or robotics no longer need to also become a frontier AI lab; the company aims to build a system 'that builds systems' and continually improves itself.
key_facts.excerpt: The lab that automates this loop will go beyond building better models. It will build the thing that is capable of continually improving itself toward any goal.

key_facts.fact: Developers can build custom agents that see, reason and take action across browser, mobile and desktop environments, improving performance for long-horizon and enterprise automation tasks like continuous software testing and knowledge work.

(NASDAQ: QCOM) and Meta today announced a strategic multi-generation collaboration for Qualcomm Technologies to be a supplier for data center CPUs for Meta. Qualcomm Technologies' data center CPU, the Qualcomm Dragonfly C1000, is planned to power Meta's next-generation server fleet.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Broadcom unveil Jalapeño, a custom LLM inference chip taped out in nine months

key_facts.fact: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled Jalapeño on June 24, OpenAI's first custom AI accelerator, designed specifically for LLM inference rather than as a general-purpose GPU
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) today unveiled Jalapeño, OpenAI's first Intelligence Processor: an accelerator architected around OpenAI's vision for the future of LLM inference, and the first AI accelerator in a multi-generation compute platform the companies are building together.

key_facts.fact: The chip went from design to manufacturing tape-out in just nine months, which the companies call the fastest ASIC development cycle ever achieved in high-performance semiconductors, aided by OpenAI's own models
key_facts.excerpt: Jalapeño was co-developed from initial design to manufacturing tape-out in just nine months, and the custom AI accelerator program represents what we believe to be the fastest ASIC development cycle ever achieved in high-performance advanced semiconductors.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI plans to deploy Jalapeño by the end of 2026 as the first step in a multi-generation chip development plan; it is a reticle-sized ASIC manufactured by TSMC

key_facts.fact: Early testing shows the first-generation accelerator will deliver performance per watt substantially better than current state-of-the-art; OpenAI says it has run its GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark model on the chip in a test environment
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says it has already begun running at least one of its prior generation models, GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark, on the chips at a workload, though in a test environment.

key_facts.fact: The partnership was originally announced in October 2025; the companies ultimately aim to deploy enough OpenAI-designed chips to require 10 gigawatts of power

stories.headline: IBM debuts world's first sub-1nm chip technology with 3D 'nanostack' transistors

key_facts.fact: The chip packs nearly 100 billion transistors onto a fingernail-sized chip, roughly twice the density of IBM's 2 nm chip unveiled in 2021, using a 3D 'nanostack' architecture that vertically stacks and staggers transistors
key_facts.excerpt: IBM's new sub-1 nm chip packs nearly 100 billion transistors onto a chip the size of a fingernail, nearly twice the density of IBM's 2 nm chip, unveiled in 2021... The nanostack design vertically stacks and staggers transistors, taking advantage of 3D sequential integration.

key_facts.fact: IBM projects the technology delivers up to 50% more performance or 70% greater energy efficiency versus its 2 nm node, and says its roadmap projects at least a decade of future scaling
key_facts.excerpt: the chip is projected to deliver up to 50% more performance or 70% greater energy efficiency compared to IBM's 2 nm node chips... IBM said its semiconductor roadmap projects at least a decade of future scaling from the new architecture.

key_facts.fact: IBM said it sees a path to production of the nanostack technology within approximately five years
key_facts.excerpt: IBM indicated it sees a path to production of nanostack technology within approximately five years.

stories.headline: Netherlands lobbies US to drop MATCH Act chip curbs that would hit ASML's China sales

key_facts.fact: Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma met US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and lawmakers in Washington to press against the MATCH Act, which would bar Chinese chipmakers from accessing chipmaking equipment
key_facts.excerpt: Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma on June 23 met with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and lawmakers in Washington, where Congress has been debating the so-called MATCH Act, which would bar Chinese chipmakers from accessing the equipment.

key_facts.fact: The most significant expansion in the US bill would curb all of ASML's deep ultraviolet immersion (immersion DUV) machines, building on existing EUV controls; ASML is Europe's most valuable company
key_facts.excerpt: Among the most significant expansions in the US bill would be curbs on all of ASML's deep ultraviolet immersion lithography, or immersion DUV, machines. That would build on existing controls of the most-advanced extreme ultraviolet lithography, or EUV, machines.

key_facts.fact: China accounted for 19% of ASML's net system sales in Q1, down from 36% in the previous quarter; the Dutch government opposes the bill, criticizing its extraterritorial character
key_facts.excerpt: China... accounted for 19 per cent of net system sales in the first quarter, down from 36 per cent in the previous quarter... The Dutch government opposes the bill, criticising its extraterritorial character as it is imposing restrictions on another country's sovereign trade policies.

key_facts.fact: Sjoerdsma said the visit was 'exceptional' and would be followed by further meetings to press US officials to reconsider; the bipartisan MATCH Act was proposed in April
key_facts.excerpt: The Match Act, a bipartisan bill proposed in April, would make it harder for Chinese chipmakers to produce AI semiconductors, in part by setting up mechanisms to coerce allied countries to keep more equipment from China.

stories.headline: IAEA chief Grossi says Iran nuclear inspections 'going to happen' despite Tehran pushback

key_facts.fact: IAEA director general Rafael Grossi said inspectors will carry out inspections in Iran under its preliminary peace agreement with the US, telling reporters in Japan 'The inspections will indeed take place.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The inspections will indeed take place," International Atomic Energy Agency director general Rafael Grossi told reporters in Japan. "We will be working on the modalities - dates, procedures, places - very soon."

key_facts.fact: Grossi pushed back against Tehran's claim that no agreement had been reached to inspect bombed enrichment sites, citing the signed US-Iran framework deal, and said 'Whether this happens the day after tomorrow or in one week or in 10 days... This is going to happen.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Obviously, to do that, we will have to inspect. Whether this happens the day after tomorrow or in one week or in 10 days, it's important, but not essential. This is going to happen," he added.

key_facts.fact: On June 23, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said UN inspectors were not scheduled to examine the nuclear sites struck by the US and Israel, directly contradicting remarks by US VP JD Vance the prior day.
key_facts.excerpt: On Tuesday, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei told reporters in Tehran that UN inspectors were not scheduled to examine the nuclear sites struck by the US and Israel last year, directly contradicting remarks made the day prior by US Vice President JD Vance.

key_facts.fact: Under the 14-point memorandum of understanding, the US and Iran committed to negotiating a final deal within 60 days, with Iran reaffirming it would never produce nuclear weapons and the US committing to lift sanctions and support a reconstruction fund of at least $300 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the terms of the framework deal, Iran reaffirmed it would never produce nuclear weapons, while the US committed to lifting sanctions and supporting a reconstruction fund of at least $300 billion (€258.5bn).

stories.headline: Russia hit by worst nationwide fuel shortages in years as Ukraine drones black out Sevastopol

key_facts.fact: As of June 24, at least 55 of Russia's 83 federal entities were reporting government or private restrictions on gasoline and diesel sales, per an RFE/RL tally, driven by Ukrainian drone strikes on oil terminals, refineries and pipelines.
key_facts.excerpt: As of June 24, at least 55 of Russia's 83 federal entities -- regions, republics, krais, oblasts, and so-called federally-designated cities -- were reporting either mandatory, government restrictions on gasoline and diesel sales, or restrictions imposed by private companies operating fuel stations, according to an RFE/RL tally.

key_facts.fact: Analysts estimate more than 20% of Russia's total refining capacity has been knocked offline; the IEA called the level of disruption 'unprecedented in the history of the Russia-Ukraine conflict.'
key_facts.excerpt: Analysts estimate that more than 20 percent of Russia's total refining capacity has been knocked offline. "This level of disruption is unprecedented in the history of the Russia-Ukraine conflict," the International Energy Agency said in a report this week.

key_facts.fact: A Ukrainian air attack on Russian-occupied Crimea knocked out power in Sevastopol, the peninsula's largest city, after drones struck its main power substation overnight; trolleybuses were halted and residents asked to keep children home.
key_facts.excerpt: A Ukrainian air attack on Russian-occupied Crimea has knocked out power in its largest city, Sevastopol, Moscow-installed governor Mikhail Razvozhayev says. Ukraine says its drones struck the city's main power substation overnight.

stories.headline: FDA approves Ionis triglyceride drug, Gilead's first-line breast cancer ADC, and GSK oral antibiotic

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Ionis Pharmaceuticals' TRYNGOLZA (olezarsen) to reduce triglycerides and the risk of acute pancreatitis in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia, a once-monthly self-administered autoinjector.
key_facts.excerpt: Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc.(Nasdaq: IONS) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved TRYNGOLZA (olezarsen) as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides (TG) and the risk of acute pancreatitis in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG: TG greater than or equal to 500 mg/dL).

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 CORE and CORE2 studies, TRYNGOLZA cut fasting triglycerides 49%-63% (50 mg) and 55%-72% (80 mg) versus placebo at six months, with a pooled 85% reduction in acute pancreatitis events at 12 months.
key_facts.excerpt: TRYNGOLZA demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in fasting triglycerides of 49%-63% (50 mg) and 55%-72% (80 mg) compared to placebo at six months. Additionally, TRYNGOLZA demonstrated a statistically significant 91% (50 mg) and 76% (80 mg) reduction in acute pancreatitis events at 12 months, with a pooled reduction of 85%.

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Gilead's Trodelvy (sacituzumab govitecan), a Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate, for first-line treatment of unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
key_facts.excerpt: Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Trodelvy (sacituzumab govitecan-hziy), a first-in-class Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (mTNBC).

key_facts.fact: The FDA also approved GSK's Utebzi (tebipenem pivoxil), the first and only oral carbapenem antibiotic, for complicated urinary tract infections including pyelonephritis, based on the noninferior PIVOT-PO Phase III trial.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved GSK's Utebzi (tebipenem pivoxil), an oral antibiotic, for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTIs)... the first and only oral carbapenem antibiotic for appropriate adults with complicated UTIs.

key_facts.excerpt: Ueda stated that the monetary policy path will remain on the upside, citing risks to inflation overshooting the 2% target... There is risk underlying inflation may overshoot 2%.

key_facts.excerpt: Prosus today announces a €400 million (US$460 million) investment into the European health and insurance tech leader, Alan, valuing it at €5.5 billion (US$6.3 billion). The investment will consist of both primary and secondary equity.

stories.headline: SpaceX launches 24 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg on a record-flying booster

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched 24 Starlink V2 Mini broadband satellites to low Earth orbit aboard a Falcon 9 from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on the evening of June 24, 2026, on the Starlink 17-45 mission.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX launched 24 Starlink broadband satellites into low Earth orbit aboard a Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Wednesday evening, June 24, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The flight used first-stage booster B1081 on its 25th flight, which landed on the droneship 'Of Course I Still Love You' in the Pacific Ocean about 8.5 minutes after liftoff.
key_facts.excerpt: the flight utilized the first-stage booster known as B1081, making its 25th successful flight... the rocket's first stage returned to Earth and landed in the Pacific Ocean on the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You" roughly 8.5 minutes after liftoff.

key_facts.fact: The mission was the 74th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, with 59 dedicated to Starlink; the constellation maintains nearly 10,700 active satellites in orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: this mission represents the 74th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, with 59 of those operations dedicated to expanding the Starlink megaconstellation network. The Starlink network currently maintains nearly 10,700 active units in orbit.

key_facts.fact: Liftoff was from Space Launch Complex 4E at 8:19 p.m. PDT (0319 UTC June 25), the seventh of eight Vandenberg launches SpaceX planned for June as it focuses Starship operations at Cape Canaveral.
key_facts.excerpt: Liftoff of the Starlink 17-45 mission from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California is scheduled for 8:19 p.m. PDT... Wednesday's mission is the seventh of eight launches SpaceX plans from Vandenberg in June.
